_about: Print settings for the v6 parts, read by cad/slice.py. Values are OrcaSlicer's own keys and value formats (filament keys are lists). Layering: the system presets named here, then 'process'/'filament', then 'supports' (or enable_support 0), then the part's 'settings'. 'plates' are parts printed together, sliced into one project; one process slices a plate, so its parts share supports and settings, and the plate holds its own 'copies'. cad/slice.py writes 'orient', 'copies' and 'settings' back here when a project was saved from the GUI. A part's 'support_enforcers' are boxes [x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1] in its model frame (mm), added to the project as support-enforcer volumes; with support_type normal(manual) the part is supported inside them and nowhere else. Every copy is laid square to the bed, its walls along X and Y; a part's 'spin' (0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees, default 0) is its quarter turn there, and a quarter turn saved from the GUI is read back into it. Spec: cad/PRINT_LIST.md, Global print settings + Supports are the slicer's job. 'variants' are parts of a non-default build (e.g. HIP_YOKE_VARIANT=glued) that the default table leaves out; cad/slice.py --variant <name> slices them.

feet.note: both feet on one plate, sole down

torso_frame.note: the torso's first print: the torso (support in its windows only), the pelvis and the battery door; the covers do not fit beside the torso, so they are torso_covers

torso_covers.note: the torso's second print: both covers, outer face down, no supports

girdle_neck.note: the shoulder girdle (support in its windows only) and the neck floor (no supports) on one plate

hip_yoke_glued.note: HIP_YOKE_VARIANT=glued: the hip yoke as two support-free U-channels, snapped and glued (cad/v6/hip_yoke_glued.py)

hip_yoke_glued_roll.note: on edge, model -Y (the y -10 bed face) down; no supports, no brim

hip_yoke_glued_pitch.note: on its back, model -X (the x -14 bed face) down; no supports, no brim

ankle_link_glued.note: ANKLE_LINK_VARIANT=glued: the ankle link as a conformal cradle and a fork, printed without supports, snapped and glued (cad/v6/ankle_link_glued.py)

ankle_link_glued_cradle.note: bottom down (the four walls' flat bottom); no supports, no brim

ankle_link_glued_fork.note: on edge, model -Y (the y -14.5 face) down; no supports, no brim

ankle_link.note: on its back (model +X up), the rear tine on the bed: the grip screws' teardrop roofs assume print-up = model +X (ankle_link.py). Supports under the web and the front tine

arm_fore_v6_L.note: on its back, web face down

arm_fore_v6_R.note: on its back, web face down

arm_upper_v6_L.note: on its back, web face down

arm_upper_v6_R.note: on its back, web face down

front_cover_v8.note: outer face down, corner blocks rising; no supports

head_face.note: flat, outer (+X) face down, camera bosses up; the outer-face pocket is then a ~50 x 44 mm ceiling 1.8 mm up, so supports (PRINT_LIST says none: open question). head.py PRINT_ORIENT_FACE = eye(3) stands it on edge; the STL is in the assembly frame

hip_yoke_v6.note: on edge, model -Y on the bed; 5 mm outer brim

leg_link_v6.note: on its back, web face on the bed

neck_floor.note: flat, bottom face down. It prints on the girdle_neck plate, whose manual supports go only inside enforcer boxes: it has none, so it prints unsupported.

pelvis_v8.note: ceiling down, cell walls rising. It prints on the torso_frame plate, whose manual supports go only inside enforcer boxes: it has none, so it prints unsupported.

power_cover_v8.note: outer face down, corner blocks rising; no supports

battery_door_v8.note: outer face down, the ribs and the tongue rising. It prints on the torso_frame plate, whose manual supports go only inside enforcer boxes: it has none, so it prints unsupported.

shoulder_girdle_v6.note: base down. Supports in its wide windows only: manual supports, snug, from the part, inside the enforcer boxes (shoulder_girdle_v6.support_enforcers(): the four trapezius-web windows and the neck tube's aft window, each box 0.25 inside the window's faces and 0.3 into its top). Everything else prints unsupported.

torso_v8.note: deck top down. Supports in its wide windows and the battery door's opening only: manual supports, snug, from the part, inside the enforcer boxes (torso_v8.support_enforcers(): every window whose flat top spans more than an 8 mm bridge, each box 0.25 inside the window's faces and 0.3 into its top). Everything else prints unsupported.

yaw_bearing_housing.note: the face against the pelvis down

yaw_carrier_v6.note: horn-plate face down, bay walls rising. Supports in the servo-plug window only: manual supports, snug, from the part, inside the one enforcer box. The lip (a 1.1 mm ledge) and the screw holes print unsupported.

support_enforcers.note: the servo-plug (connector) window through the rear wall: its ceiling in print, a 1 mm bar spanning 22.8 mm, stands on the window sill. The box keeps 0.25 inside the wall's outer face (x -19.95) and short of the idler seat's detent channel (x -16.95, y +-11.10), which has no sill: support there would run down to the bay floor
